problem: A jet ski traveled $3\,960$ meters at a constant speed of $660$ meters per minute. For how long was the jet ski in motion?

feedback.problem: It takes $6$ hours for a plane to fly $3\,450$ miles at a constant pace. How long does it take for the plane to fly $115$ miles?
feedback.worked_solution:
Speed is a special unit rate applied to moving objects. It is defined as *the distance traveled per unit of time*:

$$
\text{speed}=\frac{\text{distance}}{\text{time}}
$$

To find the speed, in miles per hour, we divide the number of miles, which is $3\,450,$ by the number of hours, $6.$ This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3\,450}{6} & =3\,450÷6 \\  & =575.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the speed of the plane is $575$ miles per hour. 

To find the time it takes the plane to cover $115$ miles, we divide the distance by $575.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{time} & =\frac{\text{distance}}{\text{speed}} \\  & =\frac{115}{575} \\  & =\frac{115÷5}{575÷5} \\  & =\frac{23}{115} \\  & =\frac{23÷23}{115÷23} \\  & =\frac{1}{5} \\  & =0.2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, it takes the plane $0.2$ hours to travel $115$ miles.
